narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 62.6% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is above 50%, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

Three factors drove this outcome, ranked by importance. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.40 was the strongest influence, but it pushed the prediction toward failure. Even though this GPA is higher than the 3.23 average among accepted students, the model has learned that students with similar grades in this dataset tend to struggle with the bar exam.

Your performance in your third year of law school was the second most important factor and worked in your favor. Placing in the 9th decile (well above the 5.79 average of accepted students) pulled the prediction toward passing. However, this positive signal was not strong enough to overcome the other influences.

Your upper-middle family income was the third most important factor and increased the likelihood of failure. While 45% of accepted students also come from upper-middle income families, the model associated this background with a slightly higher risk of not passing the bar on the first try.

To improve your chances, focus on strengthening skills directly linked to bar exam success. Consider targeted bar preparation courses, practice exams, or additional academic support before reapplying. This approach addresses the specific areas the model flagged as risks for you. (218 words)
